title: A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the geometric generalized Lax conjecture: a polynomial of degree 20 in 23 variables, built from the Choi–Lam biquadratic form, is hyperbolic, and no linear matrix inequality of any size describes its hyperbolicity cone. Hyperbolic polynomials and Gårding's convexity theorem, the Choi–Lam form and the absence of dominated bilinear squares, a positive map and the slices of the cone, the obstruction to every pencil through a norm identity and its first variation, and OpenAI's exact lift of the same cone as the projection of a spectrahedron of size 100 with 307 auxiliary variables.

units.title: A positive map and a hyperbolic polynomial
No linear matrix inequality describes the cone

prerequisites: linear algebra over R and C: determinants, adjugates, eigenvalues and orthogonal diagonalization of real symmetric matrices
derivatives of matrix-valued functions; Rouche's theorem from complex analysis
